Widget X Review 2026: What It Does Well and Where It Falls Short

Affiliate disclosure: this page contains affiliate links. If you buy through them we may earn a commission at no extra cost to you. Opinions are our own.

What Widget X actually is

Widget X is a small desktop utility that watches the folders you point it at and keeps a versioned copy of every file that changes. It runs in the background, uses almost no memory while idle, and stores its history in a plain folder you can open without the app. We installed it on a three-year-old laptop and a new desktop, pointed it at a documents folder with about forty thousand files, and left it running for three weeks. Setup took under five minutes on both machines. The first full scan of the large folder took eleven minutes; after that, changes were picked up within a few seconds. Restoring an earlier version of a file is a right-click away and worked every time we tried it, including for files that had been renamed in between.

Who it fits, and who should skip it

It fits people who work with a lot of documents, spreadsheets or design files and have been burned by an accidental overwrite. Writers, students, freelancers and small office teams will get the most out of it, because the history is per file and easy to browse. It is a poor fit if you mainly need a full-machine backup: Widget X does not image your system drive, does not back up applications, and its cloud option is an add-on that costs extra. People who already pay for a cloud drive with built-in version history may find it redundant, although its local history is faster and does not depend on an internet connection. If your files live mostly in a database or inside a single large project file that changes constantly, the version history grows quickly and you will want to tune the retention settings on day one.

How it compares

FeatureWidget XAlternative
Local version historyYes, per file, unlimited on the paid planDepends on the cloud drive; often 30 days
PriceOne-time purchase, free updates for a yearMonthly subscription

Our verdict

For the specific job of never losing a version of a document again, Widget X is the simplest tool we have used, and the one-time price makes it easy to justify. It is not a backup product and it should not replace one. Buy it if you edit a lot of files and want an undo button that reaches back weeks; skip it if what you really need is a copy of your whole computer somewhere else. The free trial is fully functional for fourteen days, which is enough time to see whether the history size stays reasonable for your kind of work.
